items.headline: Southend cabinet decides today whether to tear out Three Shells Lagoon and restore the beach
items.summary: Removing the fenced-off seafront lagoon near Southend Pier would cost about £800,000, a decade after it was built for nearly £2m.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet will decide today, Monday 16 November, whether to remove Three Shells Lagoon on the seafront near Southend Pier and return the site to a natural beach. A report to the meeting recommends removal as the most practical long-term option after a technical assessment of the alternatives, and the BBC reports the work would cost about £800,000.

The lagoon opened in July 2016 at a cost of nearly £2m, most of it public money: £1.25m came from the government's Coastal Communities Fund and the council put in £600,000, while Adventure Island owner Philip Miller contributed £100,000. It has been fenced off for most of this year after a mother and daughter had to be rescued with ropes in March when they became stuck in waist-deep sand. The council has already spent £90,000 trying to tackle complaints of a bad smell and to improve drainage, and its report says seaweed and algae have built up in the water.

Cllr Matt Dent, cabinet member for business, culture, music and tourism, said: "The lagoon has become a monstrosity that is no longer fit for purpose." Mr Miller, who says he offered other ways to fix it, blamed the council, telling the Local Democracy Reporting Service that a lack of maintenance "is the real reason it has come to this stage". Reform UK group leader Tony Cox called the scheme a white elephant that gave local government a bad name.
points: Government and council money paid for most of the original build
The site has been closed since a sand rescue in March
The cabinet meeting is held in public
